chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris together, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
A person in janabah should not touch a dirham or a dinar upon which the Name of Allah, Exalted is He, is written.

key_terms.اسْمُ اللَّهِ: the Name of Allah written on the object
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah touch coins that have the Name of Allah written on them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and reverence for the Name of Allah. It states that a person in the state of janabah should not touch coins bearing the Name of Allah, indicating the sanctity of the divine Name in matters of taharah.
